chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a man washing his wife. He said: Yes, from behind the garment; he must not look at her hair nor at anything of her.
And the woman may wash her husband, because when he dies she remains in a waiting period from him; but when she dies, her waiting period has ended.
And about a woman who dies on a journey while there is with her no mahram and no women, he said: She is buried as she is in her clothes.
And about a man who dies while there is with him no mahram and no men, he said: He is buried as he is in his clothes.

key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person within the unmarriageable kinship category
key_terms.شَعْرِهَا: her hair, specifically mentioned as not to be looked at
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period connected here to the legal bond after death
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَاءِ الثَّوْبِ: from behind a garment, without direct exposure
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُ: to wash the deceased body ritually

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife perform ghusl for their deceased spouse, and what happens if someone dies in travel without a mahram or same-gender attendant?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings on washing and burying the deceased in cases involving spouses and travel. It states that a husband may wash his wife only from behind a garment without looking at her body, and that a wife may wash her husband. It also rules that when a deceased person has no suitable same-gender or mahram person present during travel, the body is buried clothed as it is.
